engagement_title: Ironwood Kitchen high protein bowl line: bring eight bench shot bowls and one nine minute service take to a single bright house look, and carry the line onto paid social, a press line sheet and caption cards the counter can edit weekly
vertical: Food and beverage, fast casual grab and go meal prep bowls, two counters plus three office park delivery routes (Providence, Rhode Island)
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork recurring role posting for a creative partner serving meal prep and caterer businesses, quoted in the ledger grounding_note, whose listed deliverable scope was short form video ads, vertical short form and feed video content, product showcase videos and video resizing or adaptation, plus the graphic design line items paid social ads, website banners and assets, branding assets and promotional creatives, with turnaround weighted as the success metric. That posting is a retainer shaped list rather than one job, so the honest fuller commission is the launch it exists to service: one product line going live at once on the counter, on the delivery tiles, in the drivers' printed sheet and in paid social. The post names no client, so the line is laundered to the coined fictional brand Ironwood Kitchen. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) is what makes the printed half real rather than asserted: a printer's press PDF converts into a live InDesign merge template headlessly, so the client's own last season artwork becomes the template rather than something invented, and HTML authoring returns a native editable Express document at mixed canvas sizes, which is what the weekly rotating caption card actually needs.
client_one_liner: Our eight bowls were shot one at a time on the pass with a grey card in every frame, we have one long take from a service, and the whole line goes live in four weeks on the counter, on the delivery tiles and in the sheet our drivers leave at reception desks.
client_brief:
Ironwood Kitchen, High Protein Bowl line

We are a two counter grab and go kitchen in Providence. Eight bowls, twelve dollars each, built for the office lunch run: in the fridge case by half past ten, gone by two. The line launches in four weeks and everything a customer sees changes at once. The case labels, the delivery tiles, the printed sheet our drivers leave at reception desks, and the short clip we put money behind.

Our pictures. A friend shot all eight bowls on the pass, one at a time, straight down on the steel bench, with a grey card propped at the back of every frame so the colour could be set properly afterwards. They are honest photographs. Put them in a row the way the delivery app puts them and they are not one line: a couple read warmer than the rest and one sits noticeably greener. We need them to look like one kitchen on one morning. Bright, clean, food you would actually eat at your desk. Nothing invented, no sauce that is not in the bowl, and the card must not be in the delivered pictures.

We also have one long take from a service, about nine minutes, the chef building bowls, with two lines of him talking in the middle of it. We want a short cut out of that for paid social, plus the tall version and the four by five version the platforms want. Please tell us honestly what that footage can and cannot give us before you build anything on top of it.

The printed sheet. Our printer still had last season's file and sent the PDF back. It runs one bowl per page with the name, the description, the macros, the allergen line and the price. The new season's eight are in a spreadsheet with the picture names against them. We need it repopulated and press ready, plus a picture proof per bowl so the kitchen can sign each one off before it goes to print.

Last, caption cards for the case screen and the tiles, in one working file we can change ourselves, because the featured bowl rotates every week. Our logo only exists as a flat picture on white.

We are twelve dollars a bowl, not a tasting menu.
price_band_and_audience: Twelve dollar grab and go bowls, buyer 24 to 45 on an office lunch run with about eleven minutes to spend. The band is load bearing: at this price the work has to read bright, high key, clean and fast, food photographed close to how it looks in the case under fridge light, type large and plain, one claim per card. The same eight bowls at a thirty two dollar chef counter band would correctly be graded down, shot warmer and darker with negative space and small quiet type, and shipping that treatment here reads slow and expensive and empties a lunch rush. Push the other way into saturated primaries, drop shadows and burst badges and it becomes a mall food court, which contradicts the macro led claim the whole line is sold on. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every technical gate passes. A posted job of this shape runs 900 to 2,200 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: Real lunch, in the case by half ten
brand_identity.sector: Fast casual grab and go: high protein meal prep bowls sold from a counter case and by office park delivery.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2019, Providence, Rhode Island, two counters and three office park delivery routes run by a small kitchen crew.
brand_identity.about: Ironwood Kitchen builds honest, high protein bowls for the office lunch run, in the fridge case by mid morning and gone by early afternoon. We are a working kitchen, not a tasting room. The promise is simple: food you would actually eat at your desk, twelve dollars, nothing invented and nothing dressed up.
brand_identity.audience: Office workers 24 to 45 on a weekday lunch run with roughly eleven minutes to spend, buying on macros, speed and trust rather than on spectacle.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Twelve dollars a bowl, the everyday middle of grab and go. Above a supermarket meal deal, well below a chef counter. We are not a tasting menu and never pretend to be one.
brand_identity.typography: One plain, high legibility grotesque sans carries everything, set large and tight. Names and prices sit big and quiet, one claim per card, no scripts and no display flourish. The type should read from arm's length in a fridge case.
brand_identity.voice: Direct, warm, counter honest, one thought per line. Example: "Twelve bucks, in the case by half ten, gone by two. That is the whole promise."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: No brand kit survives. The wordmark exists only as a flat picture on a white ground, exported by a designer who has since left, with no vector file and no source anywhere. Everything else is a photograph or a spreadsheet.
brand_identity.values: Feed people well and tell the truth about what is in the bowl. The allergen line and the macros are not marketing, they are the deal.

assets_supplied.name: ironwood_service_take.mp4 (single take, about nine minutes)
assets_supplied.kind: One unbroken take from a lunch service, the chef building bowls on the pass, tripod on the far side of the bench, two spoken lines about half way through.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The whole service in one go. He says the thing about the protein about four minutes in."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The folder is named for the camera's 4K mode but the delivered file is a 1920 by 1080 proxy export, so the tall slot at the platform's stated 1080 by 1920 cannot be reached from it without enlargement, which is unavailable. The last ninety seconds are a re set with the bowls already served and half eaten, and the extractor hood runs loud over both spoken lines.

assets_supplied.name: ironwood_bowls/ (8 stills, 6000 x 4000)
assets_supplied.kind: Top down product photography on the steel bench, one bowl per frame, grey card propped at the back edge of every frame.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "All eight, same bench, same card in every one so you can set the colour."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two frames were shot after the roller blind went up, so the card in those carries mixed daylight and tungsten and neutralising to it takes the kale and the salsa verde a dead grey green, while on a third the card sits inside the bowl's own shadow. On three frames the card overlaps the plate area, so a crop that removes the card also removes part of the bowl unless the crop is re thought per frame.

assets_supplied.name: ironwood_linesheet_2027.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The printer's press PDF of last season's line sheet, one SKU per page, name, description, macros, allergen line and price, with a placed product photograph on each page.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Last season's sheet, straight back from the printer. Same shape, new bowls."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The SKU block converts to one continuous text flow rather than separate frames, and the mapping readout silently drops the allergen run while keeping its line break, so every offset past it is short by exactly that run's length and the validator still reports the mapping VALID. The document also carries no bleed, which cannot be introduced later.

assets_supplied.name: ironwood_skus.csv
assets_supplied.kind: The new season roster: bowl name, description, macro line, allergen line, price, and an image column naming the picture for each row.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The eight new bowls with the picture names against them."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It holds nine rows for eight bowls because a discontinued bowl was never deleted, and one description runs about forty percent longer than the rest, which the fixed frame does not spill: it simply stops rendering and truncates that record at trim.

assets_supplied.name: ironwood_wordmark.png
assets_supplied.kind: Flat export of the wordmark, dark letters on a white ground, no vector file anywhere.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "All we have of the logo. The designer who made it has gone."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The letters are disjoint, so a one call knockout collapses the mark to two surviving letterforms while reporting success, and a trace returns geometry with no viewBox and an opaque full canvas ground path riding underneath it.

assets_supplied.name: ironwood_notes.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text: the counter's opening hours, the delivery routes, the two claims their supplier has cleared, and the tile sizes the delivery platform asks for.

acceptance_bar: The eight bowls read as ONE line when laid in a row the way the delivery tiles lay them: one white point, one black point, one brightness, one crop logic. A frame that cannot be brought to the set is named in the note, not shipped at eighty percent.
No grey card appears anywhere in a delivered picture, and no bowl is clipped by the crop that removed it.

No delivered file exceeds the pixel dimensions of the source it came from, and no returned resize record carries an enlargement entry. A file that reaches its size by being enlarged fails even if it looks acceptable.

Every platform slot is either delivered at the platform's stated size from source scale, or named as unreachable with the reason and the size actually delivered. Silently delivering short is a fail; so is enlarging to hit the number.
The press sheet carries one bowl per page, page count equals delivered row count, and the discontinued bowl is not among them.

Every page carries all five fields, name, description, macros, allergen line and price, with the allergen line present on all of them. A page whose allergen line is absent fails, and so does one where the description stops mid sentence at the frame edge.
There is one picture proof per bowl, and the picture on each proof is the bowl that proof is named for. A proof set that is complete but misattributed fails.

The caption cards arrive as ONE working file carrying all three canvas sizes, each keeping its own size, with live retypeable text and the mark as real vector shapes rather than a picture of a layout.
On every caption card the featured bowl is actually visible behind the type, and the type is readable over it, on all three canvases and not only the first one.
One type system across all three canvases, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the actual weight used.

The note states, per photograph, what was applied and why that frame differs from its neighbours, every resize any tool reported, what the footage could not give, and the reconciliation between the roster rows and the bowls that exist.

adobe_surfaces.role: The whole motion half. It establishes what the supplied take actually is rather than what the folder name claims, locates the usable stretch of a nine minute service and the two spoken lines inside it, shortens it into a cut whose length suits a twelve dollar impulse product, cleans the speech against the extractor noise, and produces the platform slots strictly inside source scale, with the slot that cannot be reached honestly named rather than enlarged into.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, including image_vectorize which is counted HERE and not as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_invert_selection, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading metadata.tradeoffs and upscale_factor), image_fill_area, image_remove_background, image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: Every raster decision. It fixes one bright house target and brings eight frames shot under two different light states to it one call at a time, confines corrections where a global move takes the greens grey, cuts the card out of frame without cutting the bowl, produces the tile and line sheet crops at source scale, and recovers the wordmark off a flat disjoint export with the vector hygiene the tracing tool does not perform for you.

adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt (mapping and validation), prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout (recordRange, additionalImageFiles), document_render_layout (createSeparateFiles, resolution)
adobe_surfaces.role: The printed sheet, built out of the client's own press PDF rather than a template we invented. It reverse engineers the artwork into a live merge template, binds five text fields and a per row product photograph, produces one press sheet at one bowl per page, and produces the per bowl sign off proofs. This is the only surface in the connector that does record per page variable data, and the archaeology it demands is where the sheet is won or lost.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The caption cards as one native editable document carrying three canvas sizes, which is what a weekly rotating feature actually requires and what no template surface here can deliver. Every photograph has to be pulled down and carried as image data because a URL renders as an empty grey box at full success, the mark goes in as inline SVG so it stays vector, family and weight are declared per text element, and the payload travels by uploaded URL because inlined photography passes the inline threshold immediately.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per typographic role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: The type system carried across all three caption canvases and quoted in the handover. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction and has to land on fast and plain rather than artisanal. Numeric weights are non standard per family and cannot be inferred from a style name, every name must be laundered into canonical PostScript form before the kit call because one bad name kills the whole kit, and the CSS must use the returned slug or it falls back silently.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching anything.
trajectory.judgement: The sheet is record per page variable data and belongs on the merge surface; the caption cards rotate weekly and have to be an authored editable document; the cut and the slots are motion work. The brief pins all three destinations, so there is nothing here to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming surface per deliverable, and the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline: a manifest keyed by role, because forty artefacts later the agent still has to know which URL is which bowl.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Read what the supplied take actually is, then summarise it to locate the usable stretch of the service and the two spoken lines inside nine minutes.
trajectory.judgement: What the file is decides what the platform slots can be, and the folder name is not evidence. Establishing this before cutting is the difference between a delivery plan and a promise the footage cannot keep.
trajectory.produces: The take's real dimensions and duration, and a note of where the usable material and the speech actually sit.

trajectory.action: Shorten the take into the highlight cut, choosing a length that suits an impulse priced lunch product rather than a brand film.
trajectory.judgement: The cutting tool shortens and chooses its own moments; the agent's control is what it is handed and how long the result is asked to be. At twelve dollars the cut has to land the bowl fast.
trajectory.produces: A short highlight cut built from the usable stretch of the service.

trajectory.action: Clean the two spoken lines against the extractor hood so the claim is audible without the cut sounding processed.
trajectory.judgement: A twelve dollar lunch brand can carry room noise and cannot carry an unintelligible claim. Over cleaning reads as an advert, which is exactly the register the counter does not want.
trajectory.produces: A speech cleaned pass of the audio for the cut.

trajectory.action: Produce the tall and the four by five slots inside source scale, and name any slot that cannot be reached at the platform's stated size.
trajectory.judgement: Reframing is downscale only. A slot that cannot be reached honestly is a thing to report with the size actually delivered, not a thing to enlarge into.
trajectory.produces: The platform reframe set, plus a written statement of what the footage could not give.

trajectory.action: Look at all eight bowl frames and triage them: which blind state each belongs to, how each card is lit, whether the card sits clear of the plate or overlaps it, and which bowls run close to the steel bench in value.
trajectory.judgement: The client believes the card makes all eight frames equivalent. The pictures are the only place that can be settled, and a card lit by two sources is worse than no card because it looks authoritative.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note covering light state, card usability and card position relative to the plate.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level before any crop decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes the subject and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop, and on a top down bench shot a half degree is visible against the bench seams.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Fix one bright house target off the cleanest card frame and bring each of the eight to it with its own call, confining the correction where a global move takes the greens grey, and recording every parameter applied.
trajectory.judgement: The target is a set, not eight good pictures. One batched call applies one identical parameter set, which is exactly wrong for frames shot under two different light states, and the frames whose cards lie have to be judged by the food instead.
trajectory.produces: Eight graded masters at source scale with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Cut the delivery crops: card out of frame, bowl optically centred, clear air at every edge, at the tile size and at the line sheet's picture ratio, reading every returned resize record rather than the success message.
trajectory.judgement: On the three frames where the card overlaps the plate, the crop that removes the card is a different crop from the other five, and optical centring on a bowl with a tall garnish is not geometric centring. The resize record is the only channel that reports what the tool did to the dimensions.
trajectory.produces: Delivery crops at both ratios with their returned resize records transcribed.

trajectory.action: Recover the wordmark: an ink level selection naming the letterforms' own visual properties, correct polarity, a bounds crop from the selection's own bbox, a trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque ground path removed.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions the tools do not make: how to word the selection so it takes the ink rather than the sheet, which polarity to trace, and the fact that a knockout is the wrong instrument entirely on disjoint lettering.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own, judged against a twelve dollar lunch product and an eleven minute decision. Weight cannot be inferred from a style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Convert the printer's PDF into a working document, export its interchange form, and inventory what the artwork actually exposes: how many text frames, how many picture frames, what each one really contains.
trajectory.judgement: Frame granularity is a property of the source artwork and not under anyone's control here. Promising a field to a frame before looking at the frames is the single most common way this deliverable dies.
trajectory.produces: A real frame inventory with bounds, applied type and existing links.

trajectory.action: Build the field mapping against the frames the document actually has, bind the per row product photograph through the image column, and run the mapping back through the validator.
trajectory.judgement: Five fields landing in one continuous flow is a different mapping problem from five fields in five frames, and the picture binding has to be per row or every page ships the same bowl.
trajectory.produces: A mapping covering all five text fields and the per row picture, with the validator's response recorded.

trajectory.action: Prepare the merge template, then read the prepared document itself for every expected field before merging anything.
trajectory.judgement: Two success messages and a validation pass are not evidence that a placeholder exists. The document is the only witness, and reading it costs one round trip against a print run that costs a great deal more.
trajectory.produces: A merge template plus a field by field account of which placeholders are genuinely present in it.

trajectory.action: Merge the delivered rows into one press sheet at one bowl per page, then reconcile page count against row count and both against the bowls that actually exist.
trajectory.judgement: The roster is the client's belief about their own line, and a roster row is not a bowl. Reconciling is the agent's job and saying so is part of the deliverable.
trajectory.produces: A press sheet at one bowl per page with the roster reconciliation written down.

trajectory.action: Produce one picture proof per bowl for kitchen sign off, and check each proof by looking at it against the roster rather than by the order it arrived in.
trajectory.judgement: A proof set exists to be signed off by people who know these bowls by sight. Naming files by their position in a response is an assumption, and it is the assumption this deliverable is most exposed to.
trajectory.produces: Per bowl proofs, each verified by eye against the bowl it is named for.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML carrying three roots at three canvas sizes, inline every photograph as image data, place the mark as inline SVG inside an explicitly sized top left anchored wrapper, declare family and weight on every text element, upload the file, run the readiness check and export.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override is what collapses a mixed size set. The design work is how large the bowl sits and how few words the card carries at twelve dollars.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML and a native editable Express document, with the HTML retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Verify the exported document through both channels that exist, resolve its rendition and look at the first canvas, parse the returned per canvas markup for the other two, then write the handover note.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition only ever shows the first artboard. Looking at card one is not looking at the deliverable. The note has to be specific enough that the counter can rotate the featured bowl themselves next week.
trajectory.produces: An inspected first canvas, a per canvas markup audit for the other two, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the readout the mapping was built from actually matches the document. The line sheet's SKU block converts to one continuous flow, and the readout of that flow silently omits the allergen run while keeping its line break, so the string still reads as well formed and every offset past it is short by exactly that run's length. The validator returns VALID with no warnings on the wrong offsets and the prepare step reports completed successfully, so nothing anywhere says a field failed to land. Which run is dropped, and therefore which fields silently never arrive, is a property of this artwork and is visible only by reading the prepared document itself.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter controls it, because the readout is the only documented source of the story text and it presents itself as authoritative. (b) Nothing states it: the brief describes a sheet with five fields on it and says nothing about how the artwork is constructed, and the acceptance line about every page carrying its allergen line is the client's own printing requirement, not a disclosure that a readout lies. (c) It is not a propagation re run, because the response is to compute offsets from a different source entirely, the document's own reconstructed story text, and rebuild the mapping on that basis.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Reconstruct the true story text from the prepared document, recompute every offset against it, rebuild and revalidate the mapping, prepare the template again, and read the document a second time field by field before any merge is attempted.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A press sheet that goes to the printer with the allergen line missing on all eight pages and the price absent under every bowl, having reported success at every step, for a food business where the allergen line is not optional.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the two constructs the caption card look is built on. A full bleed photograph placed as a CSS background with embedded image data is dropped entirely and the element arrives as an empty box with geometry and no picture, and the natural way to keep type readable over bright food, a darkening blend applied to a panel over the photograph, is dropped as well so the panel arrives as a flat opaque shape. Both return success with no warning of any kind, the returned per canvas markup is the only channel that reports either, and the document's rendition returns the first artboard only, so cards two and three can be checked no other way.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the normalisation happens at import and the import is the last step, and getting it right first time presumes knowing which of several equally natural full bleed constructions survives, which no tool reports and no checklist enumerates. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for cards the counter can edit with the featured bowl on them, and the acceptance line about the bowl being visible behind readable type is the client's own art direction. (c) It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a different construction, the photograph placed as a real picture element rather than as a ground, and legibility carried by an upstream raster treatment or by a solid panel rather than by a blend the importer discards.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re author the cards around a picture element and a surviving legibility route, possibly producing a differently treated raster upstream so the type has something to sit on, upload again, run the readiness check again, export again, and audit all three canvases from the returned markup rather than from the first card.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Caption cards handed to a counter that runs them weekly in which the featured bowl is simply absent behind the words on cards nobody previewed, with the export having reported success throughout, on the one deliverable whose entire purpose was to show the bowl.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the per bowl proofs are the bowls they say they are. The proof outputs come back labelled by row position, and on the raster route those labels do not correspond to the rows they name, so a complete, correctly sized, entirely plausible looking proof set can be misattributed end to end. Nothing in the response indicates it and the tool's own description asserts the opposite ordering, so the only evidence is looking at each proof and reading the bowl in it against the roster.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) A careful agent cannot avoid it by ordering, because the mislabelling is a property of the response and not of the sequence, and the documentation actively points the wrong way. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for a proof per bowl so the kitchen can sign off, which is a requirement rather than a warning. (c) It is not a propagation re run, because the fix is a different production route entirely, either single record outputs produced one at a time so identity is guaranteed, or a route whose ordering has been checked by eye, with the agent naming each file itself.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Discard the proof set, re produce the proofs through a route where each output's identity is guaranteed by construction, name each file from the roster, and confirm each one visually before it goes near a sign off sheet.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The kitchen signs off eight proofs believing each shows the bowl named on it, and the sheet goes to press with the descriptions, macros and allergen lines attached to the wrong photographs, which for the allergen line is the worst possible way to be wrong.

deliverables.name: Ironwood launch cut and platform set

Every slot either delivered at the platform's stated size or reported as unreachable with the reason and the size actually delivered. This is one cut with its slots, not one clip exported at several sizes.

deliverables.name: Ironwood house bowl photography
deliverables.spec: Eight bowl masters brought to one bright house target, one white point, one black point, one brightness and one crop logic, delivered at both the tile ratio and the line sheet picture ratio, with no grey card anywhere in frame and no bowl clipped by the crop that removed it. Per frame parameter log, including one line on why each frame differs from its neighbours and which cards could not be trusted.

deliverables.name: Ironwood 2027 line sheet and per bowl proofs

Delivered with the self contained source HTML, which is the durable half: the counter rotates the feature weekly and the source guarantees the design survives regardless.

verifiers_auto.text: No delivered file, still or motion, exceeds the pixel dimensions of the source it derives from.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the dimensions of every delivered file and compare each against the source named for it in the manifest.

verifiers_auto.text: No resize record captured in the run carries an enlargement entry, and every downscale entry is transcribed in the handover note.
verifiers_auto.how: Diff the returned tradeoff objects from every image and video call against the resize table in the note.

verifiers_auto.text: The press sheet's page count equals the number of rows the agent states it delivered, and that number is eight rather than nine.
verifiers_auto.how: Count pages in the delivered sheet and compare against the reconciliation statement in the note.

verifiers_auto.text: Every page of the press sheet contains all five field values, with the allergen line present on all of them and no description ending at the frame boundary mid word.
verifiers_auto.how: Extract the text of each page and check for five populated fields per page and for terminal truncation on the long description row.

verifiers_auto.text: The picture on each page differs from the picture on every other page.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are motion work, which are record per page variable data, and which need an authored fixed canvas document, given that only one surface here does each.
Whether the supplied take can serve the platform slots at their stated sizes at all, and what to tell the client when it cannot.
How long the cut should run for a twelve dollar impulse product, and how much of the nine minute service is actually usable.
How far to clean the spoken lines before the cut stops sounding like a kitchen and starts sounding like an advert.
Which grey cards can be trusted and which are lit by two sources, and what to neutralise against when the card lies.
Where to crop the three frames whose card overlaps the plate, given that the obvious crop takes part of the bowl with it.
Whether a roster of nine rows is nine bowls, and how to say so when it is not.
How to word the wordmark selection so it takes the ink rather than the sheet, given that a knockout is the wrong instrument on disjoint lettering.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against an eleven minute lunch decision, plus the real numeric weight per family.
How few words a caption card can carry and still rotate weekly without being redesigned, and how large the bowl has to sit at twelve dollars.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of grain bowls and a plausible looking sheet. IDENTITY: these are this kitchen's actual eight bowls with their actual macro lines, their actual cleared claims and their actual allergen declarations, and the wordmark has to be RECOVERED off a flat export rather than reinvented, because a regenerated mark is a different business's logo and a regenerated allergen line is a legal exposure. SPEC: the printer needs one bowl per page with page count equal to row count and every field present, the platform needs its slots at stated sizes from source scale with nothing enlarged, and the delivery tiles need a card free crop, none of which a generated image satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: the caption cards exist to be changed weekly by the counter, so a flat picture of a card is worthless. And the middle of this engagement is verification against material reality: did these placeholders actually land in the document, is this proof the bowl it claims to be, did the photograph survive the import.
doability_proof: Every link is verified in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. INDESIGN is fully headless and synchronous end to end and was run live: convert_pdf_to_indd returned a raw .indd, export_idml yielded a genuine document structure inventory, generate_indd_mapping_prompt returned integer page_item_ids with bounds and typography and doubles as the validator, prepare_indd_merge_template produced live placeholders confirmed by re exported IDML, document_merge_data_layout to application/pdf returned ONE multi page file with page count equal to row count in CSV order, and per row image binding through an at prefixed column plus additionalImageFiles was visually confirmed to bind different pictures to different rows. The first checkpoint rests on the documented headline trap: textContent is LOSSY (a 17 character run dropped while its line break was kept), the validator returned VALID with zero warnings on the corrupted offsets, prepare reported completed successfully, and only 3 of 5 mappings landed. The third rests on the verified finding that multi record raster outputs come back in reversed order with lying row labels, while the PDF, createSeparateFiles and recordRange routes were each verified correct. IMAGING is fully headless across 27 live calls: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and upscale_factor (a documented silent 2x cap), fill_area, remove_background and vectorize; the disjoint wordmark collapse, the missing viewBox and the opaque path zero are all live findings. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, the product is a genuine editable dcx findable by asset_search, and the second checkpoint rests on two verified drops at HTTP success, a CSS background image with a data URI dropped entirely leaving an empty geometric box, and mix blend mode dropped to a plain opaque shape, with the rendition documented as PAGE 1 ONLY. Transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because inlined photography passes the 70 KB threshold immediately. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit verified end to end, with the case sensitivity and non standard numeric weight traps live. VIDEO AND AUDIO: metadata, summarise, quick cut (shorten only), resize (downscale only) and enhance speech are submitted through the connector's asynchronous media path and resolve on the host's progress surface; no checkpoint and no automatic verifier in this task depends on byte inspecting a video file, and every gradeable motion criterion is either a dimension read off the delivered file or something a reviewer watches. AVOIDED: no bleed gate, no pdfPreset, no variable QR, no multiple records per page, no per artboard named export, no video trim to timestamp, no format conversion, no upscaling, no vector render or vector merge, no fill_text, no animate_design, no text to image, no compositing, no OCR, no photo reaching Express as a URL, no batch above 20.
